newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Netanyahu concerned about savings tax.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Netanyahu concerned about savings tax.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has reservations about a committee's recommendation that short and medium-term savings be taxed, his spokesman Shai Bazaq said.
"The prime minister these days is studying the report. He thinks several things were done very well and there are other recommendations that he has reservations about," Bazaq said.
He said Netanyahu's reservations include the proposal to tax savings.
On Tuesday a committee led by Finance Ministry Director General David Brodett presented a 100-page proposal aimed at encouraging long-term savings and stimulating investment in the capital market.
The proposals include taxing savings of less than 10 years and reducing the amount pension funds can invest in special high-yielding government bonds.
